\section*{Resumen de orientacion}
This document defines the weekly operating system for executing the international job-search strategy.

\section*{Contenido completo depurado}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Contenido completo depurado}




\subsection{Purpose}




This document defines the weekly operating system for executing the international job-search strategy.




It explains how to use:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
25_application_tracker_template.xlsx
\end{mdcode}




and how to make weekly decisions based on evidence instead of mood, anxiety, perfectionism or endless planning.




This is the final operational control layer of the system.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{1. Core operating rule}




The job search should now be treated as a measured pipeline.




The weekly question is not:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Do I feel ready?
\end{mdcode}




The weekly question is:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
What did the data show this week, and what should change next week?
\end{mdcode}




The tracker exists to prevent:




\begin{itemize}
\item applying randomly;
\item forgetting follow-ups;
\item over-researching;
\item avoiding applications;
\item over-polishing the portfolio;
\item chasing low-value roles;
\item accepting bad offers;
\item misreading silence as failure;
\item making decisions without evidence.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{2. Weekly review cadence}




\subsection{Recommended review time}




Use one fixed weekly review block:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Sunday evening or Monday morning
Duration: 45–75 minutes
\end{mdcode}




Do not review strategy every day. Daily review creates noise.




\subsection{Weekly review inputs}




Before starting the review, open:




\begin{enumerate}
\item \texttt{25\_application\_tracker\_template.xlsx}
\item Portfolio / TwinSight case study
\item LinkedIn profile
\item GitHub profile
\item Calendar
\item Notes from interviews or recruiter calls
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Weekly review outputs}




At the end of the review, define:




\begin{itemize}
\item next week’s application target;
\item next week’s outreach target;
\item follow-ups due;
\item portfolio improvements;
\item interview prep focus;
\item skill sprint focus;
\item red flags;
\item one strategic adjustment maximum.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{3. Weekly dashboard workflow}




\subsection{Step 1 — Update raw data}




Update these sheets first:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Applications
Companies
Contacts
Interviews
Offers
Weekly Metrics
Skill Sprint
Content Assets
\end{mdcode}




Do not interpret anything until the tracker is updated.




\subsection{Step 2 — Check Dashboard}




Open the \texttt{Dashboard} sheet and check:




\begin{itemize}
\item total applications;
\item A-priority applications;
\item active pipeline;
\item interviews started;
\item offers;
\item follow-ups due;
\item average application score;
\item average offer score;
\item applications by status;
\item weekly activity.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Step 3 — Identify bottleneck}




Classify the week into one of these bottlenecks:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Bottleneck & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Bottleneck & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endhead
Asset bottleneck & Portfolio/CV/GitHub not ready \\
Volume bottleneck & Too few applications/outreach \\
Targeting bottleneck & Applying to wrong companies \\
Positioning bottleneck & Profile not generating replies \\
Conversion bottleneck & Replies but no interviews \\
Interview bottleneck & Interviews but no progress \\
Offer bottleneck & Offers weak or risky \\
Execution bottleneck & Tracker not maintained \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Step 4 — Choose one correction}




Only choose one primary correction per week.




Examples:




\begin{itemize}
\item improve TwinSight case study;
\item increase A-priority applications;
\item rewrite recruiter opener;
\item verify top 10 companies;
\item practice WebGL interview questions;
\item adjust salary response;
\item stop applying to C-priority roles.
\end{itemize}




Do not redesign the whole system weekly.




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\section{5. Weekly decision thresholds}




\subsection{Application volume}




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth}}

Use a rolling 2–4 week view, not one week.

\section{6. Application quality system}




\subsection{A-priority application checklist}




Before sending an A-priority application:




\begin{itemize}
\item [ ] Role matches one of the main role families.
\item [ ] Remote scope is plausible.
\item [ ] Work authorization does not immediately block it.
\item [ ] CV variant is correct.
\item [ ] TwinSight link is included.
\item [ ] Message references company-specific fit.
\item [ ] Salary range is not obviously below target.
\item [ ] Follow-up date is entered.
\item [ ] Tracker row is complete.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{B-priority application checklist}




\begin{itemize}
\item [ ] Role is adjacent but plausible.
\item [ ] Correct CV variant used.
\item [ ] Portfolio link included.
\item [ ] Follow-up date entered.
\item [ ] No major red flags.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{C-priority application checklist}




\begin{itemize}
\item [ ] Fast application only.
\item [ ] No deep customization.
\item [ ] Do not spend more than 10 minutes.
\item [ ] Use only if volume or cashflow requires it.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{7. Weekly review questions}




\subsection{Pipeline questions}




Answer these every week:




\begin{enumerate}
\item How many A-priority applications were sent?
\item How many B-priority applications were sent?
\item Which roles produced replies?
\item Which role family produced no signal?
\item Which job boards produced useful roles?
\item Which companies need follow-up?
\item Which recruiters replied?
\item Which applications are stale?
\item Which offers or interviews require preparation?
\item Which target category should be reduced?
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Portfolio questions}




\begin{enumerate}
\item Did TwinSight become easier to understand this week?
\item Did the demo video improve?
\item Did GitHub become cleaner?
\item Did LinkedIn become more consistent?
\item Did the portfolio gain a visible proof asset?
\item Did any improvement become perfectionism?
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Interview questions}




\begin{enumerate}
\item Which interview question was weakest?
\item Which technical concept needs practice?
\item Can TwinSight be explained in 60 seconds?
\item Can AI-assisted development be explained cleanly?
\item Can salary expectations be stated without revealing the floor?
\item Can remote-from-Colombia status be explained accurately?
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Strategic questions}




\begin{enumerate}
\item Is the role target still coherent?
\item Is full-stack creeping back in?
\item Is AI tooling over-dominating the profile?
\item Is 3D art over-dominating the profile?
\item Are applications matching the salary target?
\item Is the strategy moving toward USD 3k/month?
\item Is the 12–24 month path to USD 6k/month being strengthened?
\end{enumerate}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{8. Weekly adjustment rules}




\subsection{Rule 1 — Do not pivot after one bad week}




A bad week is not enough data.




Wait at least:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
2–4 weeks
50+ applications/outreach actions
\end{mdcode}




before making major positioning changes.




\subsection{Rule 2 — Change one variable at a time}




Do not change:




\begin{itemize}
\item CV;
\item headline;
\item role target;
\item portfolio structure;
\item salary range;
\item outreach message;
\end{itemize}




all in the same week.




Change one or two variables, then measure.




\subsection{Rule 3 — Preserve the core identity}




Every adjustment must preserve:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D / Unity / Technical Visualization
\end{mdcode}




If an adjustment moves away from that, label it as fallback, not strategy.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{9. Bottleneck diagnosis}




\subsection{Asset bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item avoiding applications because materials are not ready;
\item portfolio link not shareable;
\item GitHub not clean;
\item no TwinSight demo;
\item CV still uncertain.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Choose one asset and finish it to usable quality.




Priority order:




\begin{enumerate}
\item CV.
\item LinkedIn.
\item TwinSight case study.
\item GitHub README.
\item Demo video.
\item Portfolio polish.
\end{enumerate}




Do not improve all assets at once.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Volume bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item fewer than 10 applications per week;
\item many saved jobs but few sent;
\item overcustomization;
\item too much research.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Use application blocks:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
3 blocks/week
90 minutes each
5 applications per block
\end{mdcode}




Target:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
15 applications/week minimum
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Targeting bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item roles require senior-only experience;
\item roles require EU/US authorization;
\item roles are pure full-stack;
\item roles are pure 3D art;
\item roles are low-paid local jobs.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Increase proportion of:




\begin{itemize}
\item Unity WebGL;
\item technical visualization;
\item interactive 3D;
\item digital twin visualization;
\item simulation interfaces;
\item product visualization;
\item LATAM nearshore contractor roles.
\end{itemize}




Reduce:




\begin{itemize}
\item generic full-stack;
\item generic 3D art;
\item AAA senior roles;
\item EU-only local roles before authorization.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Positioning bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item profile views but no replies;
\item recruiters misunderstand the profile;
\item replies are for unrelated roles;
\item people ask “what exactly do you do?”
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Tighten public wording:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Unity WebGL
Technical Visualization
CAD-to-Realtime
TwinSight X500
Remote contractor from Colombia
\end{mdcode}




Remove distracting emphasis from:




\begin{itemize}
\item full-stack;
\item AI engineer;
\item graphic design;
\item generic multimedia;
\item unfinished apps.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Conversion bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item replies but no interviews;
\item recruiters ask for CV then disappear;
\item portfolio not opened;
\item no technical follow-up.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Improve:




\begin{itemize}
\item first paragraph of CV;
\item TwinSight case study top section;
\item demo video;
\item GitHub README;
\item role-specific application message;
\item portfolio card clarity.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Interview bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item interviews happen but no next stage;
\item weak technical explanations;
\item AI questions create discomfort;
\item salary discussion feels unstable;
\item WebGL/Unity questions expose gaps.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Use:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
23_interview_answer_bank.md
\end{mdcode}




Practice:




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight 60-second explanation;
\item AI-assisted development answer;
\item CAD-to-realtime explanation;
\item WebGL performance answer;
\item salary expectation response;
\item contractor-from-Colombia answer.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{Offer bottleneck}




\subsubsection{Symptoms}




\begin{itemize}
\item offers too low;
\item contracts vague;
\item unpaid tests;
\item equity-only;
\item role too broad;
\item full-time contractor with employee-like control.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{Fix}




Use:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
24_offer_evaluation_scorecard.md
\end{mdcode}




Negotiate:




\begin{itemize}
\item rate;
\item scope;
\item paid test;
\item payment timing;
\item IP terms;
\item portfolio permission;
\item review after 30/60 days.
\end{itemize}




Reject if risk remains high.




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\section{13. Monthly review}




Every 4 weeks, do a deeper review.




\subsection{Monthly questions}




\begin{enumerate}
\item Which role family generated the most responses?
\item Which role family generated the best interviews?
\item Which role family generated low-quality offers?
\item Which companies were realistic?
\item Which regions were most responsive?
\item Which job boards were useful?
\item Which outreach message worked best?
\item Which portfolio asset got attention?
\item What technical gap appeared repeatedly?
\item What should be stopped?
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Monthly decision options}




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Evidence & Decision \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Evidence & Decision \\
\midrule
\endhead
Good response from Unity WebGL & Double down \\
Good response from technical visualization & Double down \\
Only full-stack replies & Fix positioning \\
No replies from EU & Deprioritize EU until authorization \\
Low salary LATAM only & Move higher in company tiers \\
Technical interview failures & Skill sprint \\
No interviews after 100 actions & Rewrite CV/portfolio \\
Recruiters confused & Simplify headline/about \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{14. 30-day gate}




At day 30, verify:




\begin{itemize}
\item [ ] Base CV ready.
\item [ ] At least one role-specific CV ready.
\item [ ] LinkedIn updated.
\item [ ] GitHub cleaned.
\item [ ] TwinSight case study shareable.
\item [ ] Portfolio MVP live or shareable.
\item [ ] Tracker active.
\item [ ] First applications sent.
\item [ ] Outreach started.
\item [ ] Demo video at least drafted.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{If not complete}




Do not scale applications yet.




Extend setup by 7 days.




\subsection{If complete}




Move to volume + feedback phase.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{15. 60-day gate}




At day 60, verify:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Metric & Target \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Metric & Target \\
\midrule
\endhead
Applications & 50–90 \\
Outreach actions & 40–80 \\
Recruiter conversations & 3–8 \\
Interview processes & 2–5 \\
Portfolio iterations & 4–8 \\
Skill artifacts & 2–4 \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{If no replies}




Likely issue:




\begin{itemize}
\item targeting;
\item positioning;
\item CV;
\item portfolio top section.
\end{itemize}




Do not assume personal failure.




\subsection{If replies but no interviews}




Likely issue:




\begin{itemize}
\item portfolio clarity;
\item role mismatch;
\item weak proof link;
\item CV not specific enough.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{If interviews but no offers}




Likely issue:




\begin{itemize}
\item technical explanation;
\item salary mismatch;
\item AI disclosure;
\item role seniority mismatch;
\item interview preparation.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{16. 90-day gate}




At day 90, choose one:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Path & Trigger \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Path & Trigger \\
\midrule
\endhead
Continue & Interviews/offers active \\
Improve portfolio & Repeated proof gap \\
Increase volume & Low application volume \\
Refine targeting & Wrong roles replying \\
Add fallback & Cashflow pressure \\
Skill sprint & Repeated technical failures \\
Accept offer & Offer meets threshold \\
Reject/pause & Offers risky or dilutive \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Day-90 decision rule}




Use tracker evidence only.




Do not decide based on:




\begin{itemize}
\item one rejection;
\item mood;
\item comparison with other people;
\item anxiety about age;
\item perfectionism;
\item fear of applying;
\item dislike of one interview.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{17. Anti-dispersion rules}




\subsection{Project freeze}




During the active job-search phase, do not start:




\begin{itemize}
\item new flagship project;
\item new game;
\item new app;
\item new full-stack product;
\item new AI system;
\item new portfolio redesign;
\item new course path without artifact.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Allowed work}




Allowed:




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight improvement;
\item ARA README/demo cleanup;
\item portfolio MVP;
\item GitHub cleanup;
\item demo video;
\item interview prep;
\item small skill artifacts;
\item targeted company verification.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Course rule}




No course is allowed unless it produces one public artifact.




Examples:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Course work & Required artifact \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Course work & Required artifact \\
\midrule
\endhead
Unity profiling & before/after note \\
Shader Graph & small visual mode demo \\
Rebelway & FX clip or breakdown \\
German & CEFR checkpoint \\
Python automation & script/demo \\
WebGL & optimization note \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{18. Response interpretation rules}




\subsection{Silence}




Silence usually means:




\begin{itemize}
\item timing;
\item volume;
\item mismatch;
\item ATS filtering;
\item hiring freeze;
\item role closed;
\item not enough proof;
\item no referral.
\end{itemize}




It does not automatically mean the profile is invalid.




\subsection{Rejection}




A rejection is useful only if categorized:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Rejection reason & Action \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Rejection reason & Action \\
\midrule
\endhead
Too junior & Add proof / target lower \\
Not authorized & Filter region \\
Not enough Unity & Add Unity proof \\
Not enough WebGL & Add WebGL proof \\
Not enough portfolio & Improve case study \\
Salary mismatch & Adjust target \\
Role filled & Ignore \\
No reason & Track only \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Positive signal}




A positive signal is:




\begin{itemize}
\item recruiter asks for CV;
\item hiring manager responds;
\item portfolio is opened;
\item interview scheduled;
\item technical question asked;
\item request for demo;
\item referral offered;
\item compensation discussed.
\end{itemize}




Track all positive signals.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{19. Tool usage recommendations}




\subsection{Do not use Deep Research for}




\begin{itemize}
\item weekly planning;
\item CV tweaks;
\item LinkedIn tweaks;
\item outreach messages;
\item interview answers;
\item offer evaluation;
\item portfolio copy.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Use Deep Research only for}




\begin{itemize}
\item legal updates;
\item immigration rule changes;
\item tax rule changes;
\item salary benchmarking refresh;
\item market shifts;
\item new role-market research.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Use mode agent only for}




\begin{itemize}
\item live company verification;
\item active job openings;
\item recruiter/contact discovery;
\item job board scraping-like collection;
\item top-30 target validation.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Do not use agent for}




\begin{itemize}
\item strategy synthesis;
\item personal positioning;
\item CV writing;
\item interview answers;
\item legal interpretation.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{20. Top-30 company verification prompt}




Use this later with mode agent.




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Verify the current live hiring status for the top 30 A-priority companies in my target list.

For each company, check:
- careers URL;
- active relevant roles;
- role title;
- location;
- remote scope;
- contractor/B2B possibility if stated;
- work authorization requirement;
- required seniority;
- language;
- salary if posted;
- application URL;
- recruiter or hiring contact if publicly available;
- date checked.

Relevant roles:
Unity Developer, Unity WebGL Developer, Real-Time 3D Developer, Technical Artist, Technical Visualization Developer, Simulation Developer, Digital Twin Visualization Developer, XR Developer, Tools Developer, Python Automation Developer.

Do not write strategy.
Return tables only.
Do not infer worldwide remote unless explicitly stated.
Mark unavailable information as “not found”.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{21. Weekly dashboard anti-patterns}




Do not:




\begin{itemize}
\item update the tracker only when motivated;
\item leave applications without follow-up dates;
\item count saved jobs as applications;
\item count portfolio polishing as applications;
\item count course watching as skill progress without artifact;
\item re-plan the whole strategy every week;
\item change role positioning after one rejection;
\item use low-quality volume to feel productive;
\item ignore low compensation red flags;
\item accept unclear contractor terms.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{22. Final weekly operating statement}




Every week must produce measurable movement in at least three of these areas:




\begin{enumerate}
\item applications;
\item outreach;
\item follow-ups;
\item portfolio/GitHub proof;
\item interviews;
\item skill artifacts;
\item offer evaluation.
\end{enumerate}




If a week produces only research, planning or course consumption, it is not a productive job-search week.
